newsitem.title: UK: W.African lifters dismayed by Nigerian July prices.
newsitem.headline: W.African lifters dismayed by Nigerian July prices.

text.p: West African crude was steady in thin discussion as dismayed lifters of Nigerian barrels pondered the announcement of what they called overvalued Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) contract formulas for July.
"Everyone is shellshocked," said a trader. "The prices are too high by 10 to 15 cents."
"But of course we can scream and shout but it won't make any difference. The only people who suffer are us."
NNPC reduced the formula prices by between one and 19 cents a barrel from June, traders said.

Bonny Light was cut by 16 cents to Dated Brent +26 cts, Forcados was lowered by one cent to Dated +11 cents and Brass River went down by 50 cents to +31 cents. Bonny Medium was down one cent to parity with Dated.
"These prices are maybe not too unfair for the July cargoes that remain unsold but they do not reflect the value for the month as a whole," another trader said.
"Half the trades have already happened at a lower level to where the market is for the second half of July."
On the Mediterranean market, a lifter of Algerian Saharan Blend agreed a contract value at "just below" a 40-cent premium to benchmark Dated Brent for July, a trader said on Thursday.
"Let's call it done at just below 40 cents," the trader said without elaborating.
The level, agreed in talks in London with Algerian oil company Sonatrach, appears in line with recent market talk which forecast July values in the upper 30s.
Business was quiet with Urals assessed by some traders at around dated -85 cents/-95 cents.
The Virginia Two carrying 75,000 tonnes of Urals and loading at the end of June was rumoured to have moved at Dated Brent -92 cents on Tuesday or Wednesday.
The Biruinta loading June 27-29 was heard moving to an end-user at Dated -95 cents.

Urals has firmed from -$1.15 a week ago because of fears of delays in preparations for a resumption of exports of Iraq's Kirkuk sour crude under the second six-month phase of the U.N. "oil-for-food" programme. -- William Maclean, London newsroom +44 171 542 7646
